2027-02-22.title: Third Monday of the Great Fast
2027-02-22.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Serving in the newness of the Spirit
2027-02-22.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). In the Latin calendar today is the feast of the Chair of St Peter.
2027-02-22.verse: you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.
theo: The third week of the Great Fast is often the hardest. The first fervour has cooled, Easter is still far off, and the fast can quietly turn into a list of rules kept with a tight jaw. Paul speaks straight into that danger. He uses an image his readers knew well: a married woman is bound to her husband while he lives, but if he dies she is free. In the same way, he says, “you have died to the law through the body of Christ, so that you may belong to another, to him who has been raised from the dead in order that we may bear fruit for God.” The old life produced fruit “for death”; the new life belongs to the risen Christ. And he sums it up: “But now we are discharged from the law, dead to that which held us captive, so that we are slaves not under the old written code but in the new life of the Spirit.” Our fasting can be kept in either way. It can be the old written code, counted and checked like a ledger, or it can be the new life of the Spirit, a heart that gives up small things because it belongs to Someone. In many parishes these weeks bring the Lenten retreat, the dhyanam: a few evenings of preaching, adoration and confession, when people who seldom come to church find a place at the back. Its whole purpose is to move us from the ledger to the Spirit.

In the Gospel a scribe, impressed by Jesus' answers, asks the question every religious person must face: “Which commandment is the first of all?” Jesus answers with the prayer every pious Jew said morning and evening: “Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one; you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.” He adds a second, which no one had asked for: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” The scribe agrees wholeheartedly; to love God and neighbour, he says, “is much more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.” Jesus looks at him and says, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” Not far is a beautiful word and also a warning. One can know the right answer and still stand at the door. The fast is not a burnt offering by which we pay God; it clears the heart so that love may have room. The Latin Church keeps today the feast of the Chair of St Peter, the apostle whose whole authority rests on one answer given by the lake: “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you” (John 21:15).
outline: Ask: is my fast a ledger, or a love?
Point 1 · Not under the old written code
Dead to the law, alive to Christ.
The first commandment and the second.
Point 3 · Not far from the kingdom
Knowing the answer and stepping inside.
“You are not far from the kingdom of God.”
live: Say the first commandment slowly each morning this week, and let it decide one choice of the day.
If your parish has a Lenten retreat, attend at least one evening, and bring someone who has stayed away.
2027-02-22.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you have freed us from the old written code and given us the new life of the Spirit. Do not let our fast become a ledger of rules, but a love that gives itself. Teach us to love the Father with all our heart, soul, mind and strength, and our neighbour as ourselves, and do not leave us standing near the door of your kingdom, but bring us in. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the two commandments meet: we offer ourselves to the Father with Christ, and we receive the Bread that makes us one body with our neighbours.

quick: Paul: we serve in the new life of the Spirit, not under the old written code.
Jesus: love God with all your heart, and your neighbour as yourself.
Not far from the kingdom is not yet inside it.
2027-02-22.action: Let the first commandment decide one concrete choice today.
2027-02-22.question: Is my fast a set of rules, or an act of love?

family.explain: A teacher asked Jesus which rule was the most important of all. Jesus said: love God with your whole heart, and love your neighbour as much as you love yourself. All the other rules are there to help us do these two things.
family.intention: We pray for those who are attending Lenten retreats this week.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one way each of us can love God, and one way we can love a neighbour, before tomorrow?”

illus: For thirty years a man in Kottayam drove his wife to church every Sunday and waited in the car outside, reading the newspaper. He knew the prayers and could argue theology with the parish priest. On the second evening of the parish Lenten retreat a heavy rain came down, and he ran inside to take shelter at the back. He heard a preacher say: you can know every answer and still be standing outside. The next evening he came in without the rain.

pm.open: Lord, you have set us free in the new life of the Spirit. Teach us to love with our whole heart. Amen.
share: The new life of the Spirit (Romans 7:6). Where has my faith become only a set of rules?
With all your heart (Mark 12:30). What part of my heart have I kept back from God?
You are not far from the kingdom of God (Mark 12:34). What step would bring me inside?
interc: For the Church, that her laws may always serve love.
For all who are preaching and attending Lenten retreats.
For those who stand at the door of the Church and do not come in.
For the Pope, successor of Peter.
For our group, that we may love God and one another with our whole heart.
pm.close: Father, you ask of us one thing: to love you and our neighbour. Pour out your Spirit on us, so that our fast may be a gift of love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, we are in the third week of the Great Fast, when good resolutions grow tired. Paul reminds us that we have died to the old law through the body of Christ, so that we may belong to the risen Lord and serve in the new life of the Spirit (Romans 7:4–6).

A fast can be kept like a ledger: so many days without meat, so many prayers counted. Or it can be kept like a love: small gifts offered by a heart that belongs to Christ. Only the second bears fruit for God.

A scribe asks Jesus which commandment is first. Jesus answers: you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength; and you shall love your neighbour as yourself (Mark 12:30–31).
The scribe understands, and Jesus tells him: you are not far from the kingdom of God (Mark 12:34). Let us not stay near the door. This week, let one choice each day be decided by love. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said the most important rule is to love God with all your heart and to love others as you love yourself. Can you do one loving thing for God and one for someone at home today?

intro: Theme: “you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.”
The new life of the Spirit, the two great commandments, and the scribe who was not far from the kingdom.

q: Hear, O Israel: The LORD is our God, the LORD alone. You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might.
you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.
points.apply: Say the first commandment each morning this week before you speak to anyone.

points.h: The new life of the Spirit
sub: Dead to the law through the body of Christ.
Fruit for death, fruit for God.
A fast kept with a new heart.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
But now we are discharged from the law, dead to that which held us captive, so that we are slaves not under the old written code but in the new life of the Spirit.
points.apply: Choose one Lenten practice you keep grudgingly, and offer it today as a gift of love.

q: For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
When Jesus saw that he answered wisely, he said to him, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” After that no one dared to ask him any question.
points.apply: Take the step you have been postponing: confession, reconciliation, or a return to Sunday Qurbana.

concl: The fast is not a ledger of rules but a heart set free to love.
Love God with everything, love your neighbour as yourself, and do not stay at the door.
2027-02-22.resolve: Let one decision each day this week be made by the first commandment.
